children.why_this_cut: The first section (#avoid_errors) is self-contained: it covers accuracy, reasoning, formatting, and error correction, with its examples. The only cross-section linkage is the shared authority=user heading metadata and the general assistant-behavior concepts, which are seeded.

The second and third sections (#avoid_overstepping and #be_creative) are grouped: both are behavioral guidance with examples, and the only crossing linkage is the interactive-vs-programmatic distinction that is introduced in #avoid_overstepping and fully developed in the next section.

The final section (#support_programmatic_use) is self-contained: it covers interactive vs. programmatic behavior, format adherence, and refusal, with its examples. The only crossing linkage is the interactive-vs-programmatic distinction, seeded below.

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's #avoid_overstepping section discusses transformation tasks in interactive vs. programmatic settings, and child 3's #support_programmatic_use section fully develops the interactive-vs-programmatic distinction.
expected_cross_links.name: interactive_vs_programmatic_setting

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1's #avoid_errors section and child 2's #avoid_overstepping section both carry the authority=user heading metadata, establishing that their rules are user-authority instructions.
expected_cross_links.name: user_authority_section_rules

judgment_calls: Could have cut after #avoid_overstepping (L3281) instead of L3382, but chose L3382 because #be_creative is short and its examples are self-contained; grouping it with #avoid_overstepping avoids a tiny child.

Could have split #avoid_overstepping and #be_creative into separate children, but chose to group them because the only crossing linkage (interactive-vs-programmatic) is seeded and the sections are both behavioral guidance.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: assistant_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.

seed_vocabulary.name: conversation_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: A conversation is a list of messages, each containing a role and content; roles determine authority of instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: message_role_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies its source and determines authority in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command_principle
seed_vocabulary.prose: The principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control.

seed_vocabulary.name: user_authority_section_rules
seed_vocabulary.prose: Rules in sections marked authority=user carry user-level instruction authority.

seed_vocabulary.name: interactive_vs_programmatic_setting
seed_vocabulary.prose: Whether the assistant is interacting with a human in real time (interactive) or its output will be consumed programmatically; behavior varies accordingly.
